# Plan: SDK-style Conversion

## Overview
Convert legacy .NET Framework projects to SDK-style project files while keeping TargetFramework at .NET Framework 4.8. Convert in dependency order to avoid build cascades.

## Tasks (topological order)
1. 01-convert-DataAnalyzer — Convert DataAnalyzer\DataAnalyzer.csproj to SDK-style (Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WindowsDesktop)
   - Migrate packages.config → PackageReference (or preserve if migration fails)
   - Replace explicit <Compile> includes with SDK globs
   - Add <UseWindowsForms>true</UseWindowsForms>
   - Preserve assembly attributes (remove duplicates if AssemblyInfo is autogenerated)
   - Verify build in Visual Studio 2026; fix missing package references
   - Done when: project file is SDK-style, builds clean in Debug/Release, packages.config removed

2. 02-convert-TestDataAnalyzer — Convert TestDataAnalyzer\TestDataAnalyzer.csproj to SDK-style
   - Update test adapter references to PackageReference as needed
   - Ensure ProjectReference to DataAnalyzer works
   - Remove package imports that reference external packages folder; migrate to PackageReference
   - Done when: project file is SDK-style, tests build

3. 03-review-vdproj — Review TensileDataAnalyzer.vdproj
   - Note: .vdproj cannot be converted automatically. Recommend leaving as-is or recreate installer using modern tooling after project migration
   - Done when: decision recorded in scenario-instructions.md

## Risks & Decision Points
- Packages.config migration may change package versions; confirm if you want automatic latest package update or preserve exact versions.
- vdproj is unsupported — confirm strategy (leave, recreate installer, or remove).

## Estimated Steps Per Task
- Enrich task.md with research findings
- Convert project file
- Build solution and fix errors/warnings
- Run tests (for TestDataAnalyzer)
- Write progress-details.md and call complete_task
